title: SpaceX Catches Starship Returning from Orbit for First Time
paragraphs: After circling Earth 14 times, SpaceX's Starship spacecraft returned to Texas on November 14, where giant mechanical arms caught it in midair.
It was the first capture of a Starship returning from space, bringing the company closer to its goal of a fully reusable rocket system.
"Can you believe it?" SpaceX commentator Dan Huot shouted as the spacecraft hung above the ground. "Look at her! Baby, she's back!"
The mission began around 22 hours earlier, when the world's largest and most powerful rocket lifted off from SpaceX's launch site near the US-Mexican border.

The rocket consists of two stages: a booster called Super Heavy that provides the initial thrust, and the Starship spacecraft mounted above it. After separating from its booster, the spacecraft entered orbit and deployed 26 Starlink satellites.

However, SpaceX's ambition to recover both stages on the same mission ended in disappointment. According to the company, the booster's engines stopped firing too early during its return. Its guidance system detected that it was out of position and automatically diverted it away from the launch site. The booster then self-destructed over the Gulf of Mexico.
Engineers are investigating the cause. SpaceX had previously caught three boosters, but recovering both stages in a single mission remains a challenge.

Meanwhile, the company reported that the spacecraft's systems, including its protective heat shield, appeared to have performed well. Recovering and reusing both stages could reduce costs and allow more frequent launches.

That capability would support NASA's plans for lunar exploration. The agency is paying SpaceX billions of dollars to develop a version of Starship that can land astronauts on the moon and help establish a permanent lunar base.

In 2027, NASA's Artemis III mission is scheduled to test docking with Starship and Blue Origin's Blue Moon in Earth orbit. The agency is targeting 2028 for Artemis IV, which would mark the first crewed moon landing since the Apollo era.
SpaceX founder Elon Musk has ambitions beyond the moon: he wants a fleet of Starships to help build a city on Mars.
